source_description: Lake Tahoe is a large freshwater lake in the Sierra Nevada of the United States. At a surface elevation of 6,225 ft (1,897 m), it is located along the border between California and Nevada, west of Carson City. Lake Tahoe is the largest alpine lake in North America. Its depth is 1,645 ft (501 m), making it the deepest in the United States after Crater Lake (1,945 ft (593 m)). Additionally, Lake Tahoe is the sixth largest lake by volume in the United States at 122,160,280 acre·ft (150,682,490 dam3), behind the five Great Lakes. The lake was formed about 2 million years ago and is a part of the Lake Tahoe Basin with the modern lake being shaped during the ice ages. It is known for the clarity of its water and the panorama of surrounding mountains on all sides. The area surrounding the lake is also referred to as Lake Tahoe, or simply Tahoe. More than 75% of the lake's watershed is national forest land, comprising the Lake Tahoe Basin Management Unit of the United States Forest Service. Lake Tahoe is a major tourist attraction in both Nevada and California. It is home to a number of ski resorts, summer outdoor recreation, and tourist attractions. Snow and skiing are a significant part of the area's economy and reputation. Mountain and lake scenery are attractions throughout the year. The Nevada side also includes large casinos. name: Lake Hydra
review_id: commons:Dutch Springs (Lake Hydra) Quarry, Hanoverville Road, Bethlehem, PA (52403094274).jpg
creator: Warren LeMay from Chicago, IL, United States
label: Surface view
alt: Lake Hydra — surface view, as described by the source.
source_description: Beginning as a limestone quarry supplying limestone to a nearby cement plant in Bethlehem, Pennsylvania during much of the 20th Century, the industrial decline experienced by the rust belt during the 1960s and 1970s saw the closure of this former quarry in the mid-1970s, which subsequently flooded with a combination of storm runoff and groundwater. By 1980, the quarry had filled deep enough to make it a suitable scuba diving spot, with it opening to the public as Dutch Springs, operated by Stuart and Jane Wells Schooley, with an open water scuba diving facility, aqua park, and adventure course being located on the property around the quarry. The quarry operated until 2022, when the land was sold to a warehouse development, with the former owners being paid millions for the 95 acres of land so a development company could build two massive warehouses on the parts of the property not occupied by the quarry, with a proposal to fence the quarry off and leave it unused. However, due to the high-quality freshwater conditions in the quarry, a movement was started by divers in multiple parts of the Northeastern United States to prevent its closure. The movement succeeded in two local dive shop owners being donated the land by the developer, which will remain open for more limited open water scuba diving, under the name Lake Hydra. This photo was taken on Memorial Day Weekend in 2022, one of the last weekends Dutch Springs was open.
